content: The Founder settles the earlier question first. 'Never remade. Archive 001 stays 100. I'm sure.' He says it like signing something. 'Make that the line.'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

decisions.text: Founder decision: each Archive is never remade or restocked ('100 means 100'); wording to be checked by Legal and verified with a professional

content: Head of Product steps between Growth and Brand at the board. 'Hooks. Ninety seconds each, then Legal, then Research tells us how to settle it with data.'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

content: Research cuts in at the end. 'Run three hook variants on the same reel, a small spend or organic split, and measure waitlist signups, not views. Views are vanity. If urgency gets clicks but fewer signups, it's noise.'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

proposals.text: Hook test: 3 variants (true live count / registry proof / bench process), measured on waitlist signups not views
proposals.cost: low; any paid boost to be flagged to Finance

content: Brand taps the boxed note, LAST CHANCE - ONLY 12 LEFT, hard enough to curl it. 'This is what kills drops. Every brand screaming last chance on Instagram looks the same. We just agreed 100 means 100. The number is the urgency. We don't need to shout it.'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks
disagreement: Brand (no shouted urgency hooks) vs Growth (countdown and last-chance hooks)

content: The Designer stays out of it. They're sketching how the registry grid could be printed small on the back of the lid card: a map of all 100, the buyer's own box filled in.
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

content: The Plant Specialist checks the time and quietly texts a friend to water the test trays they sowed at home last night as a rehearsal.
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

content: Growth doesn't back down. 'Only 12 left converts. It's not sleazy if it's true. The grid literally tells us how many are left. A count that's live and real is scarcity you can check. That's your own argument from five minutes ago.'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

proposals.text: Live, true remaining-count hook driven by the registry ('X of 100 claimed')

content: Community tries to bridge. 'X of 100 claimed, linked to the registry, is proof. Last chance in capitals is pressure. Same number, different feeling.'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

content: CX remembers the gift buyer in the report who bought with a back-up gift ready. Urgency gets the nervous gift buyers to commit before they've read the remedy line, and those are the people who end up in their DMs.
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

content: Ops: 'And the count has to match the preorder cap we set in item 2. If the cap is below 100 because of painting capacity, then only 12 left of what, exactly?'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

content: Finance writes 'paid boost?' beside Research's test and circles it. Any spend has to come to them first.
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

content: Legal speaks precisely. 'Urgency and scarcity claims have to be accurate when they're seen. A static only 12 left in a reel that keeps playing after the count changes is the risky version. A live count tied to real orders, matching the cap, is much safer. Last chance only if it actually is. Verify with a professional.'
round_time: Early evening, Day 2 - PP6 continued: hooks

proposals.text: Rule: urgency/scarcity claims only if accurate at time of viewing; no static counts in evergreen reels; count must match the preorder cap
